doc.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019

title: Big band Latin and the basics club-date players should know
summary: A Tito Puente style big band plays differently; knowing a basic montuno and tumbao, as in yesterday's class, keeps Latin tunes from being watered down.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Not the metal one with the pads. So, and you know you’ve got a big band, Tito Puente, five saxes, four trombones, four trumpets, timbale, bongo, two singers you know, so it’s a full force. And that’s a different way of playing that, see? So this is what has to be first of all, taught for us, so you’re not watering down — if you know certain things a little, at least 101, in a montuno, know a couple of timbao, like we did yesterday at the class, the second thing. We did that C7 montuno with Victor. See, that’s a basic. If you could play that at any of those club dates, that’s passable and so easy you know. And the thing is taking a time out and really get involved with that.
